candidates.summary: the registry key is derived from the registering frame's raw pkgpath, so realm.Sub splits one realm's symbol namespace and strands a sub-created token
candidates.failure_scenario: grc20reg.Register takes rlmPath from cur.Previous().PkgPath(), which carries the "#sub" realm.Sub synthesizes. A realm registering under cur.Sub("a"), cur.Sub("b") and its primary cur gets three live keys for one symbol, against Register's own godoc claim that the key stops a realm registering two tokens under the same symbol. The mirror case panics: a token created under cur.Sub("vault") has origRealm == host but ID() == "host#vault.SYM.0", so the host frame's Register fails the HasPrefix check and aborts with "token must be registered from its own realm".
candidates.verify_by: two filetests in examples/gno.land/p/nt/grc20/v0/filetests, run with gno test -v ./gno.land/p/nt/grc20/v0: one registering the same symbol from two subs and the host, one registering a sub-created token from the host frame
candidates.evidence: key a: gno.land/r/demo/grc20subdup#a.SREG / key b: gno.land/r/demo/grc20subdup#b.SREG / key c: gno.land/r/demo/grc20subdup.SREG, all three registered; the host-frame case panics "grc20reg: token must be registered from its own realm" at grc20reg.gno:44
